businessType: B2B payments SaaS for mid-market finance teams (AP automation + embedded payouts). Founded 2019, total raised $26M. Revenue model: per-seat software subscription plus a take-rate on processed payment volume. Current ARR $8.0M, 50% YoY growth, 310 customers.
stage: ARR $8.0M, 50% YoY growth. Gross retention healthy at 94%. Net revenue retention fell from 110% to 100% over four quarters. Gross margin 68% (blended software + payments). New-logo win rate stable. Expansion bookings as a share of total bookings dropped from 38% to 19%. Cash runway 26 months at $480k/month burn.
ownerGoal: Reaccelerate net revenue retention back above 110% and protect take-rate margins against larger entrants; reach Series B metrics ($15M ARR, NRR >110%) within 15 months.
ownerConstraints: Funding constraint: $26M raised, 26-month runway at $480k/month burn; the next raise is gated on NRR re-expansion, so expansion economics are the headline metric.

Product constraint: cross-sell modules (embedded payouts, virtual cards, FX) exist and are technically live, but only ~30% of AP-automation customers have ever been pitched them; integration effort to activate a module averages 3 weeks of customer-side work.

Organizational constraint: 54 staff (14 engineering, 12 sales all on new-logo quota, 8 CS, 6 support, rest G&A). There is no account-management or expansion-sales function; CS is success-only and not quota-carrying.
Market constraint: two larger payments platforms have entered mid-market with aggressive take-rate discounts on high-volume tiers; they target the same finance-team buyer.
Commercial constraint: ~65% of revenue is software subscription and ~35% is payment take-rate; the take-rate line is where competitors compete on price.
immediateConcern: NRR has slid 110%→100% over a year and expansion bookings collapsed from 38% to 19% of bookings, even though gross retention is healthy at 94% and new-logo acquisition is fine. The owner believes larger competitors are undercutting take-rates and pressuring pricing and wants to cut take-rates to defend volume. But the data shows the company simply is not running an expansion motion: most customers have never been offered the cross-sell modules, and there is no expansion-quota owner. The owner must decide in 30 days whether to cut take-rates company-wide or rebuild the expansion engine before the next board update on NRR.
